plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any bid below your value risks losing the auction to a slightly higher bid, even if it's below your value, resulting in zero profit. Bidding above your value risks winning but paying more than the item is worth to you. Since this is round 1 and there is no history, I will bid my true value.

Since this is a single-round auction with common knowledge of rationality, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. In a symmetric equilibrium, all bidders will bid a fraction of their value. Given my value of $31, and knowing the maximum possible value is $20, I will bid conservatively, aiming to win against likely lower values. I'll bid $10.50, anticipating others will bid lower.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value minus a small amount. This is because any bid above your value risks winning at a loss. Bidding too low risks losing the item when it's worth acquiring. Since this is round 1 and there's no history, I'll bid slightly below my value to attempt a win at a reasonable price.
